title: Animal Structures and Their Functions
seo_title: Grade 4 Animal Structures Worksheets: Internal and External Structures and Adaptations
standard_text: Construct an argument that plants and animals have internal and external structures that function to support survival, growth, behavior, and reproduction.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on animal structures (NGSS 4-LS1-1): internal organs like the heart, lungs and gills, external structures like beaks, claws, fur and shells, and how they help animals survive. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Animal structures help them survive, grow and reproduce.
key_sub: Internal structures like the heart and lungs work inside the body. External structures like beaks, fur and claws work on the outside.
body_html:
How to think about it

Animals have structures (body parts) that help them survive, grow, behave and reproduce.

  • Internal structures are inside: the heart pumps blood, lungs or gills take in oxygen, the stomach breaks down food, the brain controls the body, and the skeleton supports the body.
  • External structures are outside: beaks, claws, fur, feathers, shells, scales, fins and webbed feet.

The shape of a structure tells you about its job. A hooked beak tears meat; a long, thin beak reaches nectar; webbed feet push water.

Example

How does a polar bear's thick fur help it?

The Arctic is very cold.

Fur traps heat.

Answer: It keeps the bear warm so it can survive.

Example

Is a fish's gill internal or external, and what does it do?

Gills are inside the body behind the head.

They take oxygen from water.

Answer: internal; takes in oxygen from water

Common mistakes

  • Saying fish breathe with lungs. Fish use gills.
  • Mixing up internal (inside) and external (outside) structures.
  • Saying an animal grew a structure because it wanted it. Say the structure helps the animal.

faq.q: What is the difference between internal and external structures?
faq.a: Internal structures are inside the body, like the heart, lungs and stomach. External structures are on the outside, like fur, beaks and claws.

faq.q: How do animal structures help them survive?
faq.a: They help animals get food, move, stay warm, breathe, protect themselves and raise young.

faq.q: How can a bird's beak tell you what it eats?
faq.a: A hooked beak tears meat, a short thick beak cracks seeds, and a long thin beak reaches nectar in flowers.
